positive.prompt: We just injected the organization into an existing codebase, bring it under the conventions: document the current state, build the conformance table, plan the refactors
Inventory the services in this brownfield repo, write the as-is HLD, LLD, and DB diagram per service, and run a gap analysis against our conventions
Plan the refactoring of this legacy monolith: contracts for every consumed API, service boundaries, a backend-driven client one API at a time, then domain typing inside each service

negative.prompt: Write the high-level design for the new subscriptions feature from the PRD
Slice the approved plan into sprints with a points capacity

evals.prompt: The brain was injected into a repo with three services and no docs. What do we do first?
evals.expected_output: An adoption plan: service inventory, service docs created, as-is HLD/LLD/schema per service with unknowns marked, baseline verification recorded, a conformance table and a boundaries verdict, then a top-down roadmap: contracts first, service boundaries, a backend-driven client one API at a time, the inside of each service, and a final docs pass; no PRD
expectations: Documents the current state before proposing refactors
Every service gets an adoption project and a baseline verification
Contracts for every consumed API are ordered before service boundaries, the client, and any domain-typing refactor inside a service
The client is moved onto backend APIs one API at a time, never in a sweep
Refactors are planned as small PRs with characterization tests
A docs pass at the end makes the documents current without deleting the old ones
